Enforce multi-factor authentication

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) adds an extra layer of security to your account by requiring a verification code in addition to your password.

This helps protect your account even if your password is compromised.

Setting Up Multi-Factor Authentication

To enable MFA on your account, you will need an authenticator app on your mobile device.

Popular authenticator apps include Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy, or any app that supports TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) codes.

Setup Steps

1. Install an authenticator app on your mobile device if you haven't already.

2. Open the authenticator app and select the option to add a new account.

3. Scan the QR code displayed on this page using your authenticator app.

4. The app will generate a 6-digit verification code that changes every 30 seconds.

5. Enter the current verification code in the Authentication Code field below.

6. Click Update to complete the setup.

Important Notes

Keep your authenticator app installed and accessible. You will need it every time you log in.

If you lose access to your authenticator app, you may need to contact your system administrator to regain access to your account.

Some authenticator apps allow you to back up your codes to the cloud. Consider enabling this feature to prevent lockouts.
